title: Gut microbiota transplantation for colonization of germ-free mice
author: Choo, Rogers
materials: tubes with screw cap (10 mL, 50 mL)

steps.title: Prepare 30% glycerol PBS
steps.instruction: Make sterile 30 % (v/v) glycerol in phosphate‑buffered saline (PBS) adjusted to pH 7.4.

steps.title: Prepare 20% glycerol PBS
steps.instruction: Make sterile 20 % (v/v) glycerol in PBS, pH 7.4.

steps.title: Prepare sterile PBS
steps.instruction: Prepare sterile PBS (pH 7.4) and store in a Falcon tube.

steps.title: Anaerobic pre‑incubation of reagents
steps.instruction: Place all three reagents (30 % glycerol PBS, 20 % glycerol PBS, plain PBS) in an anaerobic chamber for a minimum of 10 days before use.

steps.title: Prepare pre‑reduced PBS in Hungate tube
steps.instruction: In an anaerobic chamber, sterilize a Hungate tube, fill it with pre‑reduced PBS (pH 7.4), and seal it.

substeps.instruction: Seal a sterilized Hungate tube with a butyl rubber septum and screw cap; autoclave the sealed tube.
Transfer the tube into the anaerobic chamber, then use a sterile syringe and 23 G needle to add sterile pre‑reduced PBS.

steps.title: Pre‑weigh 50 mL Falcon tube
steps.instruction: Weigh a sterile, capped 50 mL Falcon tube to at least two decimal places for later use (alternatively, an anaerobic bag can be used to maintain anaerobiosis).

steps.title: Euthanize donor mice
steps.instruction: Perform humane killing of donor mice in accordance with approved ethics protocols.

steps.title: Expose gastrointestinal tract
steps.instruction: Place each mouse in supine position and make a vertical midline incision to expose the GI organs.

steps.title: Dissect cecum
steps.instruction: Isolate the cecum by performing two horizontal cuts 0.5 cm from the cecum at the ileum‑cecum and colon‑cecum junctions, then make a longitudinal incision on the cecum.

steps.title: Transfer cecum to glycerol
steps.instruction: Immediately place each dissected cecum into a 10 mL Falcon tube containing 5 mL pre‑reduced 15 % glycerol.

steps.title: Harvest cecal contents
steps.instruction: In the anaerobic chamber, lay the cecum on a sterile petri dish, longitudinally open it with a sterile scalpel, scrape the luminal material with a sterile spatula into the pre‑weighed 50 mL Falcon tube; repeat for all ceca of the same donor group and pool the material.

steps.title: Record net cecal weight
steps.instruction: Weigh the 50 mL Falcon tube containing the pooled cecal material and calculate the net weight of the material.

steps.title: Dilute with pre‑reduced PBS
steps.instruction: Add pre‑reduced PBS at four times the net cecal weight (e.g., 400 µL PBS per 100 mg cecal material).

steps.title: Homogenize suspension
steps.instruction: Vortex the mixture for 1 minute to obtain a homogeneous suspension; use a wide‑bore pipette tip to break up large pieces if needed.

steps.title: Filter suspension
steps.instruction: Place a 100 µm cell strainer onto a fresh sterile 50 mL Falcon tube (the “suspension tube”), pipette the suspension onto the strainer, let the supernatant flow for 5 minutes, then use a sterile pestle to extract remaining liquid; discard the strainer with residual material.

steps.title: Add 30% glycerol
steps.instruction: Dilute the filtered cecal supernatant with an equal volume (1×) of pre‑reduced 30 % glycerol.

steps.title: Aliquot into Hungate tubes
steps.instruction: Using a sterile syringe and 23 G needle, draw the final suspension and dispense into sealed Hungate tubes; allocate one tube per cage for each gavage day (volume per tube = (n × 75 µL) + 200 µL, where n = number of mice per cage).

steps.title: Store cecal suspension
steps.instruction: Freeze the Hungate tubes at –80 °C and keep them frozen until needed; avoid repeated freeze‑thaw cycles.
